executive_summary.summary: Managers submit employee access requests. An identity analyst validates required intake fields and verifies employee information against the HR source, then evaluates whether the request involves privileged access, sensitive systems, custom permissions, APIs, SSO, security requirements, or dependencies. Deficient requests return to the manager for clarification. Application owners decide requested access, with additional security review for privileged, sensitive, custom, or security-related access. IT provisions only after required approvals are recorded. The identity analyst then updates the ticket and evidence; requests nearing the SLA deadline are escalated, and a weekly report is prepared with audit evidence retained. AI is potentially suitable for bounded intake assistance, evidence gathering, draft recommendations, and backlog planning, but the current classifications block most decision-relevant request data from model context. Access decisions, provisioning, communications, escalations, report distribution, and record writes must remain human-approved and execute outside the model. Overall readiness score: 75/100.
primary_value_opportunities: Limit initial AI assistance to backlog planning or draft checklists using approved internal fields such as role, employment status, approval status, ticket status, and SLA due date. Do not include blocked request content or permit writes.

Create an allowlist aligned to the classifications, redact free text, and reject model payloads containing PII or blocked confidential fields. Test the filter against representative records before use.

Map each governed action to an authorized reviewer and require explicit approval before communications, decisions, provisioning, ticket writes, escalations, report distribution, or other record changes.
Have the policy owner determine why all control lookups returned empty and document applicable controls. Do not interpret the empty result as permission for autonomous processing.

Document deterministic criteria for sensitive-system and other additional-review triggers, along with the threshold for requests approaching the SLA deadline. Keep these rules authoritative outside the model.
primary_constraints: Sensitive or personally identifiable request data could be exposed to the model despite explicit context restrictions.

The full criteria for identifying custom, API, SSO, dependency, elevated, or security-related review requirements are not defined.

implementation_roadmap.title: Read-only workflow intelligence
implementation_roadmap.objective: Introduce AI assistance for summarization, evidence review, policy lookup, and gap detection without allowing workflow writes.
recommended_actions: Connect approved workflow and policy documents through governed retrieval.
Review data sensitivity and missing information findings.
exit_criteria: Analysis output passes quality, MCP operational, and evidence-grounding checks.
Business reviewers confirm the output is useful and sufficiently grounded.

implementation_roadmap.title: Human-reviewed AI recommendations
implementation_roadmap.objective: Allow AI to prepare recommendations, reviewer summaries, and approval packages while keeping decisions with accountable humans.
recommended_actions: Define reviewer roles and approval gates.
Add structured review queues for AI-prepared recommendations.
Track acceptance, rejection, and revision reasons.
exit_criteria: Reviewers can trace recommendations to evidence.

implementation_roadmap.title: Approval-gated workflow actions
implementation_roadmap.objective: Introduce controlled write actions only where approvals, policy checks, and audit logging are enforced.
recommended_actions: Implement policy checks before write-capable tools.
Require explicit approval tokens for controlled actions.
Log every write attempt, approval, and result.
exit_criteria: No write-capable tool can execute without required approval.
Audit trail is complete and reviewable.

implementation_roadmap.title: Limited automation for low-risk repeatable actions
implementation_roadmap.objective: Consider limited automation only for well-documented, low-risk steps with clear rollback and monitoring.
recommended_actions: Run parallel monitoring before autonomous execution.
exit_criteria: Automation scope is narrow and documented.
Monitoring confirms accuracy, safety, and cost expectations.

operational_controls: Require governed tool access through MCP or equivalent policy-controlled interfaces.

Fail closed when policy, evidence, or approval requirements are missing.
observability_requirements: Model provider, model name, reasoning effort, token usage, and latency.
Evaluation scores for quality, MCP operation, and evidence grounding.
